thread:
sara: Quick question — for /v1/generate if clients omit `model` or send `model: null`, what should we guarantee? do we still pick a default or return 400?
aj: Current runtime falls back to the default model (server-selected). We're planning to change that behavior in the next contract change.
sara: Right — product wants the deprecation announced so clients explicitly pin. timeline?
aj: Proposed: soft deprecation (warning header) for 6 weeks, then strict requirement after 12 weeks. see draft header: `X-Redwood-Warning: default-model-deprecation; will-be-required-in=6w`
mike: For compatibility, can we accept empty `model` and map to `default-v1` during the soft phase? that avoids 400s and keeps rollouts smooth.
kalpana: That's fine, but we need to be explicit in docs and SDKs. SDK auto-pin should start surfacing warnings.
sara: Agree. Also need to clarify response shape — if we auto-map to `default-v1`, are we guaranteed the same response schema as pinned models?
aj: Yes — pinned variants share the same API shape. Only model internals differ. However newer model family might add optional fields in `choices[].metadata`. we need a rule: optional fields are allowed, clients should ignore unknown keys.
ben: Can we add a `X-Redwood-Model-Version` response header during the soft window? helps client-side telemetry.
aj: Good call — will add header and echo `model` param when present. Example: `X-Redwood-Model-Version: redwood-default-v1`
mike: One more edge: if a client pins `redwood-default` (the alias) and we flip alias to `redwood-default-v2` during a rollout, is that considered breaking?
kalpana: If the alias semantics change behaviorally (e.g., different tokenization/stop sequences) we must treat it as breaking and give a longer deprecation window. Otherwise minor improvements ok.
sara: For comms: who owns the customer-facing email + changelog? I can draft the product note, need eng signoff for exact dates.
aj: Eng to lock the timeline by EOD Friday. I'm going to open an RFC in the docs repo with the header formats and SDK snippets.
ben: SDKs should expose `ClientOptions.autoPinDefault=false` opt-out during soft window. What do we call the env var? `REDWOOD_ALLOW_DEFAULT_PIN` ?
kalpana: I'd prefer `AUTO_PIN_DEFAULT_MODEL` to be explicit. keep naming consistent across sdks.
mike: Quick prod-safety check: any chance a 3rd-party proxy hits the endpoint without our new header support and breaks? deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: header-feature-toggle -> enabled in staging tomorrow 03:00 UTC, canary in prod Thursday.
sara: Perfect. I'll assemble a short internal FAQ: what to do if you see `X-Redwood-Warning` — steps for app teams.
aj: Also add a small code snippet to the FAQ for graceful handling:
```js
// treat unknown fields as opt-in info
const response = await client.generate({...});
for (const c of response.choices) {
  // safe access
  const info = c.metadata?.new_field || null;
}
```
kalpana: LGTM. after eng signoff we'll schedule the public changelog entry and SDK patch.
bene: tiny nit: spelling of header in the RFC should be `X-Redwood-Warning` (confirmed).
sara: thanks all — tagging @aj @kalpana for final dates. I'll post the internal FAQ + draft email once you confirm timeline. :thumbsup:
